notes: Timing numbers are indicative: this run shared a 4-CPU machine with other jobs.
Dataset operations: median and min of repeats, each repeat a calibrated loop, after a gc.collect(); garbage collector on unless the section says otherwise.
Per-call micro-benchmarks run with the garbage collector off, like timeit.
The Python under test differs from the cp312 wheels used for the footprint comparison; wheel sizes do not depend on the interpreter running this script.

micro.note: Per-call loops run with the garbage collector off, like timeit. Every scalar callable is wrapped in the same kind of lambda; the empty-lambda row is that shared overhead and is not subtracted. Vectorized rows exclude building the numpy arrays.

import_time._method: Median of 10 fresh interpreter processes per statement, in shuffled order. importtime_cumulative_ms sums the top-level cumulative times that python -X importtime reports for modules not already loaded by an empty interpreter. .pyc files exist and the OS file cache is warm, so this is a cold interpreter, not a cold disk. qoregeo is an editable install (a .pth path entry), so its import reads the repository source tree.

memory_load._method: Each case runs in a fresh interpreter after qoregeo is imported. tracemalloc counts Python allocations only; peak is the high-water mark during the load, current is what the loaded object keeps. rss_growth and peak_rss_growth come from /proc/self/status (VmRSS, VmHWM) in a second, untraced run (Linux only); they include allocator overhead and memory the allocator keeps.

stack_wheels._method: pip download --no-deps --only-binary :all: --python-version 3.12 --platform <tag> for each package, into a new empty folder each; the 'manylinux2014' variant is the platform tag the task names and picks the newest release that still ships manylinux2014 wheels; the 'manylinux_2_28' variant also allows glibc 2.28 wheels and so gets the newest releases. geopandas_with_dependencies is what pip fetches for 'pip install geopandas'. unpacked_bytes is the sum of file sizes inside the wheel (no .pyc).
